{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative or shows early signs of pessimism (e.g., sentiment < 0.00).",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if recent 7-day mean is trending downward and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent high prices if sentiment is positive (e.g., sentiment > 0.50) to avoid underestimating upward momentum.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is > 10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 10-15% unless sentiment strongly supports the spike.",
    "Avoid over-optimism after sharp price spikes: if true outcome is > 15% above forecast, reduce next period’s forecast by 5-8% to prevent overshoot.",
    "If sentiment is positive but forecast is consistently below true outcome, increase forecast by 3-5% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.",
    "For long-term horizons (>14 days), apply a 2-3% downward bias to account for lag in market reaction to sentiment shifts."
  ]
}
